subject: Onshore vs SCCs — DPIA evidence and Article 30 ledger
content:
From: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@finserve.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Onshore vs SCCs — DPIA evidence and Article 30 ledger

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week — FinServe is moving quickly on the pilot and privacy is our gating item. A couple of questions from our privacy team (see below). Can you please: (1) confirm whether Redwood can provide an onshore/within-EU deployment footprint for our account (or if the recommended approach is SCCs + encrypted export controls); (2) share an Article 30 ledger extract or example CSV we can reference in our DPIA; and (3) provide the minimal evidence packet you can share for a DPIA (KMS info, subprocessor list, retention/processing descriptions).

Specifically:
- Legal basis for transfers: do you rely on SCCs, adequacy decisions, or onshore hosting for EEA customer data?
- Subprocessors: we need a current snapshot and whether any subprocessor locations are outside the EEA.
- Article 30 ledger: sample file or description of the columns you capture (purpose, categories, recipients, legal basis, retention).
- DPIA artifacts: a one-page summary we can attach to our board paper; and any redacted logs/retention statements.

We don’t need SOC 2 material at this stage, but the DPIA team will ask for anything that makes the legal basis and transfers transparent. Ideally we can get a small artifact set by next week.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call.

Best,
Alice Jensen
Privacy Lead, FinServe

---

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@finserve.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 11:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Onshore vs SCCs — DPIA evidence and Article 30 ledger

Hi Alice — thanks, and great to hear the pilot is progressing. Short answers up-front: we support both patterns. For customers that require EU residency, we offer Private/Dedicated deployments in EU regions (customer-managed VPC or Redwood-managed within-EU capacity). For hosted customers, our contractual transfers are governed by SCCs (standard contractual clauses) combined with additional contractual safeguards (encryption at rest/in transit, access controls, and KMS integration).

I’m attaching a compact evidence bundle for DPIA triage and a sample Article 30 ledger extract. I’ve looped in Karthik for the SCC/technical details and Laura for the evidence packaging and retention queries.

Proposed next steps:
- Karthik: can you confirm the SCC baseline and any EU-only hosting options we should call out?
- Laura: can you assemble a 1-page DPIA summary and retention excerpt?
- Alice: once you confirm what level of redaction is acceptable we’ll produce a sanitized ledger extract.

Tentative delivery: Tuesday 22 Dec (assuming no further approvals). If you need faster, we can prioritize an excerpt today.

Attachments: [Attachment: redwood_subprocessor_snapshot_202612.zip (zip)] [Attachment: redwood_dpia_overview.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@finserve.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 08:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Onshore vs SCCs — DPIA evidence and Article 30 ledger

Rachel — quick notes on the legal/technical posture so Alice has clarity: 

1) Transfers/legal basis:
- Hosted (Redwood API): default contract uses EU SCCs for transfers from the EEA. We pair SCCs with technical measures: customer-controlled keys where applicable (KMS integration), encryption, and restricted admin access.
- Dedicated/Private: for customers that require residency we provision EU-only capacity (dedicated GPU pools in the EU cloud region or on-prem package). In those cases, data does not leave the region and transfer legal basis is residency rather than SCCs.

2) Article 30 ledger: we can produce an excerpt CSV with the following columns: record_id, controller_contact, processing_purpose, categories_of_data, recipients (redacted subprocessor names permitted), legal_basis, retention_period, technical_measures, transfer_basis, last_updated. I attached a sanitized excerpt for reference.

3) Subprocessors: the snapshot contains name, function, country, and transfer_basis. We can redact exact endpoints/credentials but must provide locations and high-level function (e.g., cloud compute, logging, monitoring).

4) Sampling methodology: propose we provide a 3-month sampling window plus the Article 30 ledger excerpt for the relevant project. That should satisfy most DPIA reviewers without producing full logs.

Attachment: [Attachment: article30_ledger_excerpt_202512.csv (csv)]

Happy to join the DPIA call if FinServe wants to walk through the ledger.

—Karthik
Principal Infrastructure Security Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alice Jensen <alice.jensen@finserve.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 12:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Onshore vs SCCs — DPIA evidence and Article 30 ledger

Thanks — adding a couple of packaging notes for the DPIA team at FinServe: 

- DPIA one-pager: I’ll produce a concise 1-page summary that covers processing overview, technical controls (encryption, access controls, KV cache policy), data flow diagram (high-level), and transfer/legal-basis options.
- KMS & rotation: include the KMS key rotation cadence and whether customer-managed keys are available for Dedicated/Private.
- Retention excerpt: provide a short table of default retention periods and where customers can override (via policy).

I’ve attached the KMS key rotation document and a retention excerpt you can share as-is. I recommend we mark the ledger excerpt as "Sanitized — sample" and redact specific recipient endpoints.

Attachments: [Attachment: kms_key_rotation.pdf (pdf)] [Attachment: retention_policy_excerpt.txt (txt)]

Laura Bennett
Privacy & Regulatory Programs Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2026 14:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Onshore vs SCCs — DPIA evidence and Article 30 ledger

Hi Alice — attaching the sanitized artifacts we discussed. Summary below and next steps.

What we attached:
- redwood_dpia_overview.pdf — 1-page DPIA summary (processing overview, controls, transfer posture).
- article30_ledger_excerpt_202512.csv — sanitized Article 30 ledger extract (sample rows with redacted recipient endpoints).
- redwood_subprocessor_snapshot_202612.zip — current subprocessor snapshot (includes country and function; contact endpoints redacted).
- kms_key_rotation.pdf — KMS rotation cadence and customer-key options.
- retention_policy_excerpt.txt — default retention windows and override controls.

Short summary:
- If FinServe requires EU residency for the pilot, we recommend Dedicated/Private in EU regions (no outbound transfers).
- For hosted pilots using Redwood API, SCCs + encryption + KMS provide the contractual + technical safeguards.
- The ledger excerpt and snapshot should satisfy the DPIA reviewers for legal-basis transparency; we can produce additional logs on request under an agreed redaction and sampling plan.

Next steps:
1) Alice — confirm whether you want the Dedicated/Private option priced in the pilot proposal (we can provide a cost delta).
2) Alice — confirm acceptable redaction level for publishing a fuller ledger (if the DPIA needs more granularity).
3) Neha/Laura/Karthik — please stand by for follow-up requests from FinServe privacy team; they may ask for a short walkthrough call.

Drive folder with artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcxyz-dpia-artifacts

Thanks —
Rachel Kim

Redwood Inference
